set.approach: Start at the Meysan Lakes trailhead by the Whitney Portal campground and follow that trail to the head of the drainage; overnight stays need a permit. The route sits on a nameless buttress on the hillside between Mt. Irvine and Mt. Mallory, above Meysan Lake. A short walk up boulders and talus from the lake leads into the gully below the wall.
set.descent_text: The route finishes with a blocky ridge of third to low fifth class that ends on the Irvine-Mallory divide. Hike south along the divide, then drop to Meysan Lake by the east slopes of Green Pass.

review.notes: Location, ridge finish and descent from the route page; trailhead and trail from the peak page. Single-source route page, no numbers given.

set.approach: Hike in from the Horseshoe Meadows trailhead on the Cottonwood Lakes trail system to the Tiki Face, which stands just beyond the sixth lake in the chain. The route is on the right-hand side of the face's right pillar, starting in a shallow right-facing corner.

review.notes: Approach and start from the route page; Horseshoe Meadows access from the peak page. Descent not stated: the party stopped at a pseudo-summit.

set.approach: Hike in from the Horseshoe Meadows trailhead on the Cottonwood Lakes trail system to the Tiki Face, which stands just beyond the sixth lake in the chain. The route is on the left-hand side of the face's right pillar, starting with blocky climbing off a ledge.

review.notes: Approach and start from the route page. Descent not stated.

set.approach: From South Lake, follow the Bishop Pass trail over the pass, then contour beneath Mt. Agassiz toward Mt. Winchell, staying at roughly the same elevation. Dropping slightly is easier than sidehilling the talus. Camping is possible at Dusy Basin or at the lakes by Isosceles Peak. The route starts to the right of the initial scrambling of the West Arete, and it joins the West Arete near the knife-edge section.
set.descent_text: From the summit, descend the east arete (third class), dropping to the second chute on that side and following it down, then traverse to Winchell Col without losing elevation. West of the col, take the left of the two forks and downclimb a loose gully at third to fourth class. A rappel station on the left side of the gully serves the drop-off partway down, and easier ground lies below it. The chutes on the west face are poor ways down.

review.notes: Approach, start and descent from the two route pages, which agree on the east-arete descent and the gully rappel station; rappel count and lengths deliberately left out.

set.approach: From South Lake, follow the Bishop Pass trail over the pass, then contour beneath Mt. Agassiz toward Mt. Winchell, staying at roughly the same elevation. Dropping slightly is easier than sidehilling the talus. Camping is possible at Dusy Basin or at the lakes by Isosceles Peak. The route is on the large southwest buttress, the wall far right of Silver Linings Arete. Its corner borders the Winchell Col descent gully, and the line starts on the lower-angled left part of the wall.
set.descent_text: The route continues up the south ridge to the summit. From the summit, descend the east arete (third class), dropping to the second chute on that side and following it down, then traverse to Winchell Col without losing elevation. West of the col, take the left of the two forks and downclimb a loose gully at third to fourth class. A rappel station on the left side of the gully serves the drop-off partway down, and easier ground lies below it. The chutes on the west face are poor ways down.

review.notes: Location and descent from Training Day page cross-read with the West Arete descent.

set.approach: A long hike from the Rancheria trailhead, on Wishon Reservoir's eastern shore, leads to Blackcap Basin on the White Divide, where camps are available. The route follows the west ridge of Oyster Peak, which is visible from the southern part of the basin. The start is at a buttress above a talus pile on the east shore of Pearl Lake, where the lower buttresses begin on the left; other starts are possible.

review.notes: Pearl Lake buttress from route page; Rancheria trailhead and Blackcap Basin from the journal report. No descent in either.

set.approach: Start at Wolverton in Sequoia National Park and take the trail along Long Meadow, following signs for Alta Peak and Panther Gap. After the trail crests a ridge, leave it and head toward the ridge that carries Panther Peak; a saddle just west of the peak is a few minutes on. Leave packs at the saddle and descend along the base through brush. The route is on the central buttress, right of Krymptonite; look for the high first bolt on the tilted pillar that starts it.
set.descent_text: The last pitch is easy fifth class on gear. From the top, either rappel the route from anchors at the edge of the formation, or walk off by downclimbing, walking and scrambling out along the ridge. The belays up to the last pitch are bolted for rappelling.

review.notes: Everything from the route page and area page; rope length for the rappel left out as single-source.

set.approach: Start at Wolverton in Sequoia National Park and take the trail along Long Meadow, following signs for Alta Peak and Panther Gap. After the trail crests a ridge, leave it and head toward the ridge that carries Panther Peak; a saddle just west of the peak is a few minutes on. Leave packs at the saddle and descend along the base through brush. The route is on the south face of the west buttress; follow the approach for Krymptonite but stop early, at the first larger buttress you would otherwise pass.
set.descent_text: The route ends on a small summit that is otherwise hard to reach. Rappel anchors at the back of that summit lead down into the gully.

review.notes: Route page and area page.

set.approach: Start at Wolverton in Sequoia National Park and take the trail along Long Meadow, following signs for Alta Peak and Panther Gap. After the trail crests a ridge, leave it and head toward the ridge that carries Panther Peak; a saddle just west of the peak is a few minutes on. Leave packs at the saddle and descend along the base through brush. The route starts low in the East Gully, to the right of Liquid Gravity.
set.descent_text: After the last pitch, scramble up to the anchor a short way over the lip, then walk off rightward and uphill to the summit of Panther Peak. The East Gully is also a way down from the formation.

review.notes: Route page for start and walk-off; area page for the East Gully.

set.approach: From the Pine Creek trailhead, follow the trail past Pine Lake and Upper Pine Lake to Honeymoon Lake, then continue to Granite Park. Above the lake, cut southwest cross-country up and over Royce Pass to reach the Royce Lakes basin. The route climbs the most unbroken face on the northeast side, above the largest Royce Lake, with a snow or talus approach to the base; the largest crack system is the line.

review.notes: Face and line from route page; trail from area page; basin from the journal report.

set.approach: From the Pine Creek trailhead, follow the trail past Pine Lake and Upper Pine Lake to Honeymoon Lake, then continue to Granite Park. Above the lake, cut southwest cross-country up and over Royce Pass to reach the Royce Lakes basin. Go around to the west shore of the largest Royce Lake; the orange cracks that lead up to the ridge are easy to pick out and serve as a guide.
set.descent_text: The route finishes on the summit of Royce Peak, after a long stretch of third and fourth class and easy fifth class along the ridge. A walk-off to the south leads down from there.

review.notes: Route page for start; journal report for the summit finish and south walk-off.

set.approach: From the Pine Creek trailhead, follow the trail past Pine Lake and Upper Pine Lake to Honeymoon Lake, then continue to Granite Park. Above the lake, cut southwest cross-country up and over Royce Pass to reach the Royce Lakes basin. The route begins at the toe of the large pinnacle and ridge on the east side of Royce, an easy walk from Merriam Peak; it climbs the ridge on the east face of the nearly detached spire that rises over Royce Lake.

review.notes: Start from the route page; ridge from the journal report. Descent after the second summit not described.

set.approach: The big dome beside Tenaya Lake lies just off the road, with parking all along its foot. The line runs up the middle of the broad face that sits left of West Country.
set.descent_text: Walking off is possible by heading down and left below the headwall, cutting down where the ground allows; the area's general walk-off heads up and left (west) until third and fourth class slabs lead down beside the steep headwall. Rappels are the alternative: a series of stations leads down beneath the headwall past Jabberwalky to a big sandy ledge, which suits anyone unsure of friction. Do not rappel from the trees.

review.notes: Route page and area page.

set.approach: The big dome beside Tenaya Lake lies just off the road, with parking all along its foot. The route is on the far west side of the dome, just right of Far West Country.
set.descent_text: Rappel west, down Potter in Wonderland. Avoid rappelling down the cracks, where ropes can jam. Walking off west and down the slabs beside the headwall is the area's alternative; do not rappel from the trees.

review.notes: Route page and area page.

set.approach: The big dome beside Tenaya Lake lies just off the road, with parking all along its foot. The route is on the far left side of the dome, just right of Turkey Trot.
set.descent_text: Rappel down Turkey Trot from its anchor. Walking off west and down the slabs beside the headwall is the area's alternative; do not rappel from the trees.

review.notes: Route page and area page.

set.approach: The big dome beside Tenaya Lake lies just off the road, with parking all along its foot.
set.descent_text: Rappel to the south from the fixed anchors at the base of the headwall, not back to the base of the route. Downclimbing the slab beside it is also done. Walking off west and down the slabs beside the headwall is the area's alternative; do not rappel from the trees.

review.notes: Route page and area page; location detail not given on the route page.

set.approach: The big dome beside Tenaya Lake lies just off the road, with parking all along its foot. The route is an enormous left-facing corner beside Turkey Trot, at the dome's left end, and it begins from the big sandy ledge.
set.descent_text: Walk off down and left to the west, keeping below the headwall for as long as you can before cutting down, or rappel from the hidden station under the headwall: it leads to the Jabberwalky anchor and then down Aoxomoxoa to the sandy ledge. Do not rappel from the trees.

review.notes: Route page and area page.

set.approach: Reach Miter Basin by Cottonwood Pass, Old or New Army Pass, or Arc Pass. The spires stand directly south of Sky Blue Lake in a row. Sky Blue Spire is the southernmost, on the left as you walk up Miter Basin, and the sharpest summit of the group. Sapphire Crack takes the left of two splitter cracks on the blank shield left of the summit, above a large ledge that is reached by moderate fifth class.
set.descent_text: Scramble down the summit towers at fourth class to the saddle on the north side, which belongs to the neighboring tower of the group. Continue scrambling west toward Primrose Lake, with a rappel needed at one point to reach a talus walk-off. An easy walk around the formation returns to the base.

review.notes: Route and area page; the rappel length is a single-source count and omitted.

set.approach: Reach Miter Basin by Cottonwood Pass, Old or New Army Pass, or Arc Pass. The spires stand directly south of Sky Blue Lake in a row. Sky Blue Spire is the southernmost, on the left as you walk up Miter Basin, and the sharpest summit of the group. The route follows the exposed arete, beginning with a crack and corner system that reaches a ramp.
set.descent_text: The route follows the ridge to the summit. Scramble down the summit towers at fourth class toward the saddle to the north, then continue west toward Primrose Lake, where a rappel reaches a talus walk-off.

review.notes: Route and area descent text.

set.approach: Reach Miter Basin by Cottonwood Pass, Old or New Army Pass, or Arc Pass. The spires stand directly south of Sky Blue Lake in a row. This is the second spire from the left, the next formation right of Sky Blue Spire, reached from Miter Basin. The route is its northeast ridge: get onto the ridge from the climber's right and traverse to a high point at its toe.
set.descent_text: From the summit, head back down the route a short way, then turn southeast on a large ledge toward the first spire. Two options reach the broad ledge system: a rappel on the southwest face, or a downclimb that wraps around the northern flank. Follow it around the south side of the formation to the gully between spires 3 and 4, then take scree and talus down to Primrose Lake.

review.notes: Route page and area page agree.

set.approach: Reach Miter Basin by Cottonwood Pass, Old or New Army Pass, or Arc Pass. The spires stand directly south of Sky Blue Lake in a row. The route follows the unbroken crack system, left of center, that runs the full height of the spire; approach it from Miter Basin.
set.descent_text: Head southwest toward Primrose Lake, then follow a broad ledge northwest to the notch between spires 3 and 4. Scramble down scree and talus from there to the lake.

review.notes: Route page and area page agree on the descent; the spire numbering is inconsistent across pages so the approach names no ordinal.
